correctness.rationale: For a finite commutative chain ring R with maximal ideal m=(π), |m^j|=q^{n−j}, multiplier group U abelian and G=R^+⋊U, direct conjugation gives (b,w)(a,u)(b,w)^{-1}=(wa+(1−u)b,u). If k=v(1−u), the additive orbit is one class mod m^k when v(a)≥k, size q^{n−k}, and one complete shell for each h<k, size (q−1)q^{n−1−h}; hence k+1 classes per multiplier. Summing |1+m^j| gives N+(q^n−1)/(q−1) classes and stated commuting probability. A generating additive character exists because every nonzero ideal contains the socle; the additive dual is R with unit orbits by valuation. Clifford induction from H_h=1+m^{n−h} of size q^h yields exactly q^h degree (q−1)q^{n−h−1} irreducibles plus |U| linear characters. Differences of ideal-character sums give the stated three-case formula S_(n−h)(a) and complete values, and the sum of squared degrees is |G|. For Z/8 vs F2[t]/(t³), U differs C2² vs C4 so G_ab differs C2³ vs C4×C2 even though q=2,n=3. Independently enumerated affine Z/8 conjugacy classes 1^2,2^3,4^6 (order32), Z/9 classes 1^1,2^1,3^2,6^3,9^3 (order54), and Z/4 classes 1^2,2^3, consistent with the formulas. These finite counts corroborate, not prove, the universal representation classification.
residual_risks: The character table includes multiplicative characters θ of the actual unit group, and therefore is not asserted identical across all rings with the same (q,n); only class-size and degree multisets are.
Use of standard Clifford little-group theorem and generating Frobenius character requires finite commutative chain ring; general finite local rings are outside scope.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Clifford/Mackey semidirect-product irreducible induction works for all groups with abelian normal subgroup; this is a general construction from which the representation classification follows when unit-orbit geometry is known. Wan–Zhou treats GA_n over finite F_q, not nonreduced/mixed-characteristic commutative chain rings. General ring automorphism work is not an ordinary complex character-table formula. Thus conventional representation theory is credited as the mechanism rather than novel, while explicit chain-ring valuation tables and ring-independent class/degree multisets require additional specialization.

value.rationale: A family-wide closed classification of conjugacy classes, ordinary complex character degrees and values for affine groups over every finite commutative chain ring is useful representation-theoretic structure. Uniform spectral invariants across different ring types and an exact obstruction to recovering group isomorphism from those spectra are natural questions, not an arbitrary small numeric gain; cyclic-ring cases and general induction are explicitly credited as prior mathematics.
residual_risks: The inference uses standard semidirect representation theory; the new content is ring-type-uniform explicit formulas, not a fundamentally new Clifford theorem.

limitations: Commutative finite chain rings only, not nonprincipal local/noncommutative rings.
Ring-independent only for multisets of class sizes/irreducible degrees, not entire table or group isomorphism type.
Dokchitser cyclic-ring thesis unavailable at original link; old cyclic subfamily not claimed new.
